== 3 # HB-03 · Memo: nightly lodging limit exceptions
version: 1 · status: current · effective: 2025-06-01
§1 Purpose
This memo lists group exceptions to the nightly lodging limit in HB-22. Supporting records are kept for seven years in line with the retention schedule. Managers may reject claims that are not supported by the documentation described here. This section is reviewed once a year by the finance team together with the policy owner.
§2 Exception for business trips to Zurich, Geneva or Oslo
For business trips to Zurich, Geneva or Oslo, the nightly lodging limit is 270 EUR per night instead of the standard amount. Supporting records are kept for seven years in line with the retention schedule. Audit samples are drawn every quarter, and selected employees are asked for documentation. Employees should keep costs reasonable and book through the approved channels where possible.
§3 Carve-out
The exception above does not apply to contractors; they follow the standard nightly lodging limit in HB-22 §2. Costs paid with a company card are reconciled in the same tool as personal claims. Claims are submitted in the expense tool within 30 days of the date the cost was incurred. Claims that combine several costs must list each cost on a separate line of the claim.
§4 Review
This memo is reviewed together with the main policy. Receipts must be attached for every item claimed; photographs of paper receipts are accepted. Amounts are stated in euros; conversions use the published rate

version: 3 · status: current · effective: 2026-03-01 · supersedes: HB-32
§1 Scope
This policy sets the home-office equipment allowance for all employees. Amounts are stated in euros; conversions use the published rate on the day of payment. Questions about this section go to the policy owner named in the document header. Supporting records are kept for seven years in line with the retention schedule.
§2 Standard home-office equipment allowance
Employees may claim a one-off home-office equipment allowance of 500 EUR. The policy owner may publish clarifications in the policy FAQ without changing this section. Line managers check each claim for plausibility before it is released for payment. Questions about this section go to the policy owner named in the document header.
§3 Additions
For employees who work remotely four or more days a week, 150 EUR is added to the standard home-office equipment allowance. The policy owner may publish clarifications in the policy FAQ without changing this section. Audit samples are drawn every quarter, and selected employees are asked for documentation. Line managers check each claim for plausibility before it is released for payment.
§4 Approval and receipts

== 13 # HB-13 · Travel policy: lodging
version: 2 · status: superseded · effective: 2025-06-01 to the day before 2026-02-01 · superseded by: HB-22
§1 Scope
This version set the nightly lodging limit for all employees. Receipts must be attached for every item claimed; photographs of paper receipts are accepted. Audit samples are drawn every quarter, and selected employees are asked for documentation. This section is reviewed once a year by the finance team together with the policy owner.
§2 Standard nightly lodging limit
The nightly lodging limit for business travel was 210 EUR per night, including taxes and city fees. Line managers check each claim for plausibility before it is released for payment. Audit samples are drawn every quarter, and selected employees are asked for documentation. Claims that combine several costs must list each cost on a separate line of the claim.
§3 Additions
For a stay that includes a Saturday night, 25 EUR per night was added to the standard nightly lodging limit. Any deviation from this section must be explained in the comment field of the claim. Employees should keep costs reasonable and book through the approved channels where possible. Where a local agreement sets stricter rules, the stricter rule applies for that location.
§4 Version status
This version applied from 2025-06-01 until the day before 2026-02-01. From 2026-02-01 it is superseded by HB-22; claims for earlier dates keep this version's amounts
